task.description: WF-03 Step 2b design gate on CODE-DESIGNER's ISS-0227 fix design at commit a64159d. Every C1-C5 line citation in iss0224-sandbox-pool-async-provisioning.md opened and confirmed

result.summary:
FAIL, on ONE finding (D1), narrowly scoped. Everything else in this design PASSes and was re-derived first-hand; CODE-DESIGNER must NOT rewrite the document, only replace section 4.1 and section 8 item 7, and correct two citations.

(1) LINE CITATIONS -- R1-R5 ALL CORRECT, verified by opening lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex at HEAD a64159d. R1 :160 is `           owner_pid: pid(),` inside `@typep provision_op` (:158-164). R2 :535 is `         owner_pid: owner_pid,` inside reserve_slot/2's {:provision, %{...}} literal (:531-540). R3 :316 is `  #                  schema_name: String.t()` inside the in_flight: block (:312-317) of the state-shape comment (:299-318), and :315 is `  #                  task_pid:    pid(),` -- it does carry the trailing comma the design says to drop, and :316 itself has none, so the comma instruction is correct and necessary. R4 :572 is `          schema_name: op_schema_name(op)` inside pump/1's in_flight = %{...} literal (:568-573), and :571 is `          task_pid: task.pid,` -- again the comma instruction is correct. R5 :592-593 are exactly the two `defp op_schema_name/1` clause heads and nothing else. The carve-out lines are as described: :527 `    owner_pid = elem(from, 0)` and :528 `    owner_ref = Process.monitor(owner_pid)`. ZERO wrong line citations in the removal set -- no risk of sending ELIXIR-DEV to a wrong line.

C1-C3 ALL CORRECT in lib/letflow/design/iss0224-sandbox-pool-async-provisioning.md. C1's block is :500-507 with :502 = `  owner_pid:   pid(),`. C2's block is :517-522 with :521 = `  schema_name: String.t()` and :520 = `  task_pid:    pid(),` (comma present, as stated). C3's :802 and :804 are verbatim what the design quotes, and :794's step-1 pseudocode does indeed name no fields, so the 'needs no edit. Checked.' is true. W11 re-verified by reading :525-575: the field-by-field rationale list has bullets for db_queue, in_flight, owner_ref, sandbox_id/schema_name-of-provision_op, task_ref/task_pid, owner_down? and purpose -- there is NO bullet for in_flight's schema_name and NO bullet for owner_pid, so there is no prose rationale to retract; and :559's owner_ref bullet does say 'via Process.monitor(owner_pid)', which correctly refers to the surviving local and correctly stays verbatim. C4/C5 are append/prepend instructions and are unambiguous.

(2) WRITE-ONLY PROOF, RE-RUN INDEPENDENTLY. MY OWN COUNTS, not inherited. `grep -rn "owner_pid" lib test` -> 4 lines in lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex (:160 typespec, :527 local bind, :528 local use, :535 op-literal write), 4 lines in test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs (:420 local bind, :443/:444/:445 uses of that local, all on a test-spawned pid), 2 prose lines in test/specs/ISS-0048.md, plus design-markdown prose. NO read of the field off an op anywhere. `grep -rnohE "in_flight[a-z_]*\.[a-z_]+" --include=*.ex --include=*.exs lib test | sort | uniq -c` -> 12 hits: .op x7 (:401, :447, :724, :813, :920 in lib; :1007, :1146 in test), .task_ref x4 (:386, :392, :427, :521), .task_pid x1 (:1008). ZERO .schema_name. Dynamic access: `grep -nE "Map\.(get|fetch|fetch!|take|has_key\?|pop|values|keys)" lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex` -> exactly 1 hit, :344 `Map.fetch(state.active, sandbox_id)`, on `active`, never on an op or on in_flight; bracket access `grep -nE "(op|in_flight|p)\[" lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex` -> zero hits. Destructuring: the only place any code binds a schema_name in the neighbourhood of in_flight is test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs:920 and :1007, both `{:provision, %{schema_name: o_schema}} = state.in_flight.op` -- i.e. from .op, which is the design's own section 2.3 derivation, confirming section 2.4. CONCLUSION CONFIRMED: both fields are genuinely write-only across lib/ and test/, by my measurement.

(3) CARVE-OUTS -- ADEQUATE. The surviving local at :527 and owner_ref are each fenced four independent times: section 2.1 bullets 1-2, section 6.1 (five bullets specifically on owner-monitor semantics), section 8 items 1-2, and section 7 post-change check 2, which gives the exact diagnostic ('if it reports an undefined variable at :528, the local at :527 was deleted in error'). An implementer working only from this doc would have to override four explicit prohibitions, and the failure mode is a hard compile error at :528, not a silent behaviour change. Not a plausible miss.

(4) op_schema_name/1 DECISION -- REPRODUCED, DESIGN CORRECT. I built my own throwaway mix project at scratch/cdv0227/ (mix.exs + lib/probe.ex containing one public function and the EXACT two-clause op_schema_name/1 shape being deleted, with no caller) and ran `mix compile --warnings-as-errors`. Output: 'warning: function op_schema_name/1 is unused ... lib/probe.ex:4:8: Probe (module)' then 'Compilation failed due to warnings while using the --warnings-as-errors option'. EXIT=1. The design's W7 is reproduced exactly; R5 is therefore mandatory, not stylistic, and section 3's decision is correct. Section 3.2 also independently confirmed: `ls -a .github` -> 'No such file or directory' and `git ls-files .github` -> empty, so there is genuinely no GitHub Actions definition in this repo; mix.exs:64-68 is `"letflow.check": ["letflow.check_toolchain", "format --check-formatted", "compile --warnings-as-errors", "letflow.check.test"]` with `compile --warnings-as-errors` as step 3 exactly as claimed; docs/agents/protocols/GIT_MERGE.md:166 is verbatim `      mix compile --warnings-as-errors`. I did not reproduce W8 (the elixirc probe) because it is not load-bearing for the decision -- W7 alone settles it -- and the design correctly treats W8 as a caution, not as evidence.

(5) SUPERSEDE CONVENTION -- GENUINELY IN-REPO, ALL THREE PRECEDENTS EXIST. (a) lib/letflow/design/iss-0048-sandbox-pool-owner-crash-reclaim.md:21-38 is a dated REWORK NOTICE that names a later section authoritative, states the earlier sections are 'left unedited in place as the historical record', and enumerates specifically what is superseded -- exactly as described. (b) lib/letflow/design/iss064-orphaned-tenant-schemas-fix.md:619 is `## 11. Extension (ISS-0110, 2026-08-21) -- the age-threshold filter alone is no longer sufficient`, the appended dated issue-attributed section shape the design copies. (c) iss0224-...md:38 is the R2-F2 row and it does say the deleted RT-2 assertion '(c) is kept as an explicit struck-through deleted row in the table so the audit trail lives in the table, not only in prose'. The convention is found, not invented, and section 5.1's reasoning about why a fenced code block needs a comment-line marker instead of strikethrough is sound (strikethrough does not render inside a fence).

(6) CONTESTED POINT -- SECTION 4.1 IS OVERRULED. See issue D1 and next_action; the minimum regression test is specified there in full.

(7) SCOPE AND COMPLETENESS -- PASS. NO IMPLEMENTATION CODE: the design's fenced blocks are (i) section 2.4's quotation of an EXISTING test line, (ii) section 3.3's table, (iii) sections 5.2/5.3's comment text destined for another MARKDOWN file, (iv) section 5.5's markdown heading. There is no .ex/.exs function body and no block presented as source to paste into lib/. GH#465's FOUR acceptance criteria all covered: 'both removed from SandboxPool state' -> section 2 R1-R4; 'every former use derives at the point of use, with no second stored copy' -> sections 2.2/2.3, with the honest and verified observation that there are zero former use sites, so nothing needs rewriting; 'the full sandbox pool suite (RT-1..RT-8 included) passes unchanged, no test bound moves' -> section 4's per-file table plus section 7 check 3 -- and I confirmed RT-1..RT-8 do live in test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs (the RT-1..RT-4 in sandbox_pool_call_timeout_test.exs are ISS-0220's separate numbering, and that file is also run); 'git grep confirms no remaining writer' -> section 4's stated method plus section 7 check 2. NO SILENT RE-DECISION: section 6's table addresses INV-SP-A1..A7 individually plus INV-SP-1..7, INV-SP-DOWN-1..5 and INV-SP-T1..T5; section 6.1 spells out owner-monitor semantics; section 6.2 confirms the serialized DB worker (pump/1 still spawns one async_nolink at a time, run_op/1 at :586-590 reads the op's own schema_name, untouched -- verified in the source); section 5.7 enumerates what must not be edited in iss0224-...md. Nothing ISS-0224 settled is re-opened.

(8) OQ-2 -- DISCLOSURE ADEQUATE, AUDIT NOT IN SCOPE. GH#465 names exactly two fields; a module-wide dead-field audit of drop_op()/db_queue/active is a different question with a different (unbounded) size, and expanding into it silently is the scope-creep failure this gate also guards. The disclosure is not hand-waving: it states plainly what was NOT done, refuses to claim there are no others, and section 13 item 1 reports it to ORCH as a candidate successor issue per core-directives' 'No Issue Left Local-Only'. That is the correct handling. Section 13 item 2 (the elixirc-vs-mix foot-gun as a candidate anti-patterns entry) is a genuinely useful finding and I endorse filing it.

TWO WRONG CITATIONS FOUND, both non-routing (D2, D3 below) -- neither sends ELIXIR-DEV to a wrong line, and neither on its own would have been a FAIL. Recorded because a design that sells its citations as re-derivable must have them reproduce.

issues.title: Section 4.1 (and section 8 item 7) forbid the WF-03 Step 4 regression test, leaving ISS-0227 with no legal terminal status
issues.detail: Section 4.1 declines to specify any new regression test on the ground that a test asserting a struct field's absence 'would assert this design's implementation choice rather than any behaviour of the pool', and section 8 item 7 turns that into a prohibition on ELIXIR-DEV ('Do not write any new test file'), with section 4.1 additionally telling ORCH that TEST-DESIGNER should be dispatched 'only to re-run the existing suites, not to author new cases'. That is not an omission the downstream steps can route around -- it actively blocks WF-03 Step 4. RULING: OVERRULED, on three grounds, the third of which is decisive. (i) WF-03_issue_resolving.md:99-103 requires Step 4's test to be shown to fail against the pre-fix code and pass against the post-fix code, as the proof that the fix fixed something. The doc's own escape hatch at :105-117 ('when the pre-fix failure is non-existence') does not apply here -- the module exists and the fields exist, so a genuine fail-then-pass is available. (ii) The 'it pins an implementation detail' objection mistakes the defect class for a behavioural one. ISS-0227's defect IS structural: REVIEWER filed it precisely because a second stored copy of derivable state can silently diverge, and ISSUE-FIXER's own diagnosis states that this class 'is reachable only by reading, or by a structural assertion on the exact key set'. A white-box key-set assertion is therefore not a gratuitous pin -- it is the only mechanical detector of the exact hazard the issue exists to remove, and it is the standing style of this suite, which already reaches into :sys.get_state/1 at :920, :1007, :1008, :1146 and elsewhere. Section 4.1's own objection that the test 'would have to be deleted the day the field is legitimately re-introduced' is the guard working as intended: re-introduction should require a deliberate edit that confronts ISS-0227's rationale, which is exactly what silent re-introduction is not. (iii) DECISIVE: upholding 4.1 leaves ISS-0227 with no truthful terminal status. ISSUE_QUEUE.md:180-247's vocabulary is open / in_progress / resolved / instrumented / no_defect. `resolved` (:187) requires 'a root cause was actually removed, and a regression test proves it'. `no_defect` (:199-208) is false here -- a defect existed and is being removed. `instrumented` (:192-197) is false here -- the root cause IS removed, and it would additionally demand a superseded_by successor carrying remaining work that does not exist. So a design that forbids the test forces the run either to write a false `resolved` or to leave a genuinely-fixed issue non-terminal. Section 4.1's proposed evidence (a) mix compile --warnings-as-errors exiting 0 and (b) the existing suites still passing is real and should be kept, but it is absence-of-regression evidence, not proof the root cause was removed: both (a) and (b) would read identically if ELIXIR-DEV made no change at all. MINIMUM REGRESSION TEST, specified precisely enough for TEST-DESIGNER to write. One test, no new file, appended to the ISS-0224 RT block in test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs, named 'RT-9 (ISS-0227): the in-flight provision op and the in_flight record carry no duplicate of a derivable value'. Reach the observation point with the helpers the file already has and NO sleep: pool = start_pool!(max_concurrent: 1); spawn_claimer(pool, :o, 1_000); state = wait_until_pool_state(pool, "O's provisioning is in flight", &provision_in_flight?/1) -- this is the exact synchronisation :917-918 already uses. Then assert THREE things. (1) The exact key set of the in-flight provision op: bind {:provision, p} = state.in_flight.op and assert Enum.sort(Map.keys(p)) == [:from, :owner_down?, :owner_ref, :sandbox_id, :schema_name]. Use sorted-key-list EQUALITY, not refute Map.has_key?(p, :owner_pid) -- equality is what makes it a drift guard in both directions, failing both if owner_pid returns and if some future change quietly adds another undeclared field. (2) The exact key set of the record: assert Enum.sort(Map.keys(state.in_flight)) == [:op, :task_pid, :task_ref]. (3) That the derivations still reach the values, so the case documents the replacement and not merely the removal: assert elem(p.from, 0) == the claiming pid returned by spawn_claimer/3, and {:provision, %{schema_name: n}} = state.in_flight.op with assert is_binary(n). FAIL-THEN-PASS: against pre-fix code (this branch's a64159d sandbox_pool.ex, both fields present) assertion (1) fails on :owner_pid and assertion (2) fails on :schema_name; against post-fix code all three pass. TEST-DESIGNER states both runs explicitly per WF-03:99-103. COVERAGE MAP, so nothing is left unproven: RT-9 assertion (1) proves R2, assertion (2) proves R4, assertion (3) proves the section 2.2/2.3 derivations remain reachable; mix compile --warnings-as-errors exiting 0 proves R5; the existing suites passing unchanged prove no behavioural drift. R1 (the @typep line) is compile-time only and is not runtime-observable by any test -- it is discharged by ELIXIR-DEV's diff and REVIEWER, and the design should say so rather than leave it silently uncovered. REQUIRED EDITS: replace section 4.1 with the above (keeping its (a)/(b) evidence as additional, not sole, evidence), delete or invert section 8 item 7, and add RT-9 to section 7's file table as a TEST-DESIGNER-owned change to test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs -- which also means section 7's 'Explicitly NOT touched: every test file' must be narrowed to exclude that one file. With those edits ISS-0227 earns `resolved` legitimately.

issues.title: Section 4's stated grep method does not reproduce its stated count of 32
issues.detail: W4 and section 4's Method both state `grep -rnohE "in_flight[a-z_]*\.[a-z_]+" lib test | sort | uniq -c` -> '32 hits, every one .op / .task_ref / .task_pid, zero .schema_name'. Run verbatim, that command does NOT reproduce that result, because lib/ contains lib/letflow/design/*.md: it returns roughly 50 hits, ten of which ARE `.schema_name` -- all of them prose inside iss0224-...md and iss0227-...md, none of them code. Restricted to code with --include=*.ex --include=*.exs it returns 12 hits, zero .schema_name. So neither reading yields 32. THE CONCLUSION IS CORRECT and I re-derived it independently (see result.summary item 2); only the reported figure and the command as written are wrong. This matters because section 4 explicitly offers the method 'so this is re-derivable rather than asserted', and a validator following it verbatim gets .schema_name hits and a scare. Fix: state the command with the code-file restriction and the count that command actually produces.

Three edits only: (D1) replace section 4.1 with the RT-9 regression-test specification given in issues[0], invert section 8 item 7, add test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs to section 7's file table as TEST-DESIGNER-owned and narrow section 7's 'Explicitly NOT touched: every test file' accordingly, and state that R1 is compile-time-only and discharged by diff review rather than by any test; (D2) correct :632 to :656; (D3) correct section 4's grep method to the code-restricted form and its actual count.
